summary: Hiloron, the lake republic of the giants: a council of chiefs, the memory of the crossings, the giant host and the price of stone.

lake_council.name: The Lake Council
lake_council.desc: A council of chiefs that governs slowly and honestly.

lake_council_2.name: Council of Stone
lake_council_2.desc: Decisions cut into a great stone: few care to argue with it.

memory_of_the_crossings_spirit.name: Memory of the Crossings
memory_of_the_crossings_spirit.desc: The giants carried the allied hosts in the First Age, and still carry strangers over streams.

giants_stride.name: The Stride
giants_stride.desc: A league in a quarter-hour, without tiring.

giants_stride_2.name: The Host of Hiloron
giants_stride_2.desc: The giants muster as a single host, and cross a country before the news of their marching.

shield_of_giants_spirit.name: Shield of Giants
shield_of_giants_spirit.desc: Eight-foot shields in a line: little passes, nothing passes through.

war_chiefs_spirit.name: War-Chiefs
war_chiefs_spirit.desc: Chiefs trained to command a host that cannot be told to hurry.

lake_boats_spirit.name: Lake Boats
lake_boats_spirit.desc: Great boats of lake-oak carry giants and stone alike.

giants_wake.name: The Giants Wake
giants_wake.desc: The great kin are awake, and are not in a patient mood.

the_crossings_remembered.title: The Crossings Remembered
the_crossings_remembered.desc: The Keepers of the Crossings sing of the ancient crossings, when the giants of Hiloron bore the allied hosts over rivers in flood. The song is long and slow, and the council hears it out in a silence that fills the hall.

hiloron_trade.title: Stone from Hiloron
hiloron_trade.desc: Hiloron offers Novez a better price for its stone, on the condition that Novez sends its wool and its grain in the same boats. The counsellors weigh the offer against their own quarries.

focuses.name: The Lake Council
focuses.desc: Hiloron's giants keep a lake league. A council of chiefs governs under the Charters, slowly and honestly, in a hall built for those who stoop under no door.

focuses.name: Chiefs of the Shore
focuses.desc: Each shore-town sends its chief to the council, and each chief brings a retinue of a dozen giants. The hall is crowded, and the debates are short.

focuses.name: The Long Memory
focuses.desc: The giants remember the crossings of the First Age war, when their forebears carried the allied hosts across rivers on their shoulders. The Keepers of the Crossings sing it every year.

focuses.name: Council of Stone
focuses.desc: The council's decisions are cut into a great stone at the water's edge, so that any giant may read them by passing. Few care to argue with a stone.

focuses.name: Law of the Lake
focuses.desc: The shore-towns agree a single law of the lake: free passage of boats, fair weights and a quarrel judged by three chiefs, never by one.

focuses.name: The Council Endures
focuses.desc: The lake council has sat in the same hall for a thousand years. It does not expect to move, and it does not intend to be hurried.

focuses.name: Memory of the Crossings
focuses.desc: The giants carried the allied hosts across the rivers of the First Age, and the memory has become a point of honour. A giant of Hiloron will carry any stranger across any stream, and expect no thanks.

focuses.name: Songs of the Alliance
focuses.desc: Giants sing the old songs of the alliance in the long evenings, in voices that rattle the rafters. The songs are about friendship, crossing rivers and the quality of bread.

focuses.name: Keepers of the Old Ways
focuses.desc: The Keepers of the Crossings guard the lore of the giants: the names of fords, the words of oaths and the shape of the old war. They write it on stone and recite it from memory.

focuses.name: The First Men Remembered
focuses.desc: The giants recall the First Men, who fought beside them in the old war and whose line was said to have ended. The Keepers are no longer quite so sure that it did.

focuses.name: Hear the Stranger
focuses.desc: A stranger stands before the council and warns them of a darkness in the south. The giants hear him out in silence, as they hear everything, and then begin to count their stones.

focuses.name: An Old Debt Repaid
focuses.desc: The giants carried the First Men once, across the river that could not be crossed. They will carry the Heir now, and the debt is paid in the only coin they trust.

focuses.name: The Giant Host
focuses.desc: The giants of Hiloron are few, but each is the match of six men. When the council calls them, they come to the lake in their stone-nailed boots, and the earth shakes.

focuses.name: Hurlers of Stone
focuses.desc: A giant can throw a boulder a hundred paces with the casual flick of one arm. A company of them behind a wall is a siege-engine that does not need winding.

focuses.name: Great Mauls
focuses.desc: The giants carry mauls of oak shod in iron, taller than a man and heavier than a horse. A strike from one is a thing felt in the next valley.

focuses.name: The Stride
focuses.desc: A giant covers a league in a quarter-hour, and does not tire. The host of Hiloron can cross a country before the news of its marching.

focuses.name: Shield of Giants
focuses.desc: Shields of lake-oak, twice a man's height and bound in iron, are carried in a line by giants side by side. Little passes them, and nothing passes through.

focuses.name: War-Chiefs
focuses.desc: War-Chief Gorrum the Tall schools a company of chiefs in the art of commanding a host that cannot be told to hurry. They learn that a giant moves when he agrees to, and not before.

focuses.name: The Host of Hiloron
focuses.desc: On the council's word, the giants muster as a single host, stone against iron and lake against land. It is small, and nothing stands before it for long.

focuses.name: Lake and Quarry
focuses.desc: The lake gives fish and the quarries give stone, and Hiloron's craftsmen have learned to turn both into silver. The council takes care that they do not forget it.

focuses.name: The Quarries
focuses.desc: New galleries are driven into the quarry faces, and the giants haul out blocks that no cart could carry. The Golden Court wants the stone, and has begun to haggle over the price.

focuses.name: Lake Boats
focuses.desc: Great boats of lake-oak ply the shore towns, built to carry giants as easily as stone. A passing merchant would mistake one for a barn on the water.

focuses.name: Stone Roads
focuses.desc: The giants lay roads of great flat stones, each a cartload by itself. Such a road will outlast every empire that crosses it.

focuses.name: Trade with Novez
focuses.desc: Hiloron's neighbour Novez has long bought its stone from the giants at a price that both find irritating. The council offers a better arrangement.

focuses.name: A Rich Shore
focuses.desc: Stone, fish and trade make Hiloron the richest shore of the south-west. The giants spend their wealth on better boats and heavier hammers, which is what giants do.

focuses.name: The Old Charter
focuses.desc: The Charters of Parim recognise the lake league as a dominion, with its own council and its own laws. The giants have honoured them for centuries, and expect the same.

focuses.name: Levies of Giants
focuses.desc: Hiloron sends a few of its giants to serve the Concord, in places where one giant is worth a company. The Royal Army finds them hard to feed and very hard to replace.

focuses.name: The Giants Wake
focuses.desc: The council has called the great kin from the quarries and the lake-shore. The giants have woken, and they are not in a patient mood.

focuses.name: Stones Against the Dead
focuses.desc: Boulders thrown by giants break the dead as they break anything: into smaller pieces. The giants fight the hosts of the grave with the same stolid method they bring to quarrying.

focuses.name: The Lake Holds
focuses.desc: Walls of giant-cut stone rise around the lake towns, each block the size of a cottage. If Hiloron is to fall, it will take a great while.

focuses.name: Charter and Shield
focuses.desc: Hiloron reaffirms its place in the Concord and offers the Lost Cause a company of its great kin. The giants do not forget a bargain, and the Golden King is held to his half.

focuses.name: Hiloron Endures
focuses.desc: The war is over, the lake is still and the great kin go back to their quarries. The council sits again in the old hall, and the Keepers sing the crossings once more.
